name: manual_189690
claim: After fixing a process-substitution exit-status blind spot (a producer wrapped in '< <(...)' whose failure a while-read loop can't see), check every remaining stage of that same data flow for the identical gap -- a partial fix that only materializes the FIRST producer to a file can still leave a SECOND filter stage (awk, a second python3 call) wrapped in its own swallowing process substitution.

decisions.notes: orama PR #298: fixed 'git cherry | awk' silently treating a failed enumeration as zero unique commits by writing git cherry's output to a temp file first -- but the awk filtering step right after was still '< <(awk ... "$file")', the identical bug one level down. CodeRabbit's follow-up review caught it. Fixed properly by eliminating the awk subprocess entirely (parse the already-materialized file with bash parameter expansion), which also removes the second subprocess's own failure surface.
